name: ⭐ Laurie Clark — Movement, Circle Games & Singing Games
detail:
USA (Denver, Colorado). Waldorf early childhood educator for more than four decades. Lead kindergarten teacher at The Denver Waldorf School, Director Qualified in the state of Colorado. Mentors Waldorf teachers across the country and teaches in several Waldorf teacher training programmes internationally including the West Coast Institute (BC, Canada) and Sunbridge Institute (New York). National and international conference presenter. Faculty at Dancing Hands & Frolicking Voices (with Lynn St Pierre). Laurie's work centres on singing games, circle time, developmental movement and the four foundational senses — touch, life, self-movement and balance — and how to support their healthy development in young children.

📚 Books (both with Nancy Blanning, WECAN Publications):
• Movement Journeys and Circle Adventures, Volume 1 (2006, Nancy Blanning & Laurie Clark). The foundational text. Contents: Introduction to the Foundational Senses · The Developmental Movement Exercises (zoo exercises) · Equipment list · Movement Journeys for Autumn, Winter, Spring, Summer and Anytime. "A book of genius and a gift to young children. The games are brilliantly thought out to bring children into the world with strength and balance." — Kim John Payne
• Movement Journeys and Circle Adventures, Volume 2 (Nancy Blanning & Laurie Clark). All-new songs and movement activities developing healthy senses. Includes nursery rhyme movement, bean bag games, seasonal suggestions, environment preparation and what is happening "under the surface." Addresses the observation that "children are having difficulty finding their way into physical life in a harmonious way, into a sense of well-being. The body is not a comfortable home where they can feel relaxed and safe" — and offers specific therapeutic movement as remedy.
• Singing Games for Families, Schools and Communities — Anna Rainville & Laurie Clark. WECAN Publications. A treasury of singing games weaving movement, song, community and seasonal rhythm for all ages.

🎓 Training & Teaching: Faculty at Dancing Hands & Frolicking Voices (dancinghandsfrolickingvoices.org) · West Coast Institute (BC, Canada) · Sunbridge Institute (NY) · Denver Waldorf School's Nurturing the Roots Therapeutic Course · national and international early childhood conferences

✨ Co-teaching partner: Works closely with Lynn St Pierre (Dancing Hands & Frolicking Voices) and Nancy Blanning (co-author, Denver Waldorf School therapeutic education). The Denver Waldorf School community has produced some of the most significant Waldorf therapeutic movement resources in North America.

name: ⭐ Suzanne Down — Juniper Tree School of Story and Puppetry Arts
detail:
USA (Boulder, Colorado). The foremost Waldorf puppetry educator in the world. Juniper Tree School of Story and Puppetry Arts was founded over 40 years ago and has now trained 30+ groups of professional puppeteers. Suzanne's journey began at Emerson College in England where she studied hand puppetry with the legendary Gisela Bittleston. She went on to found Juniper Tree Puppets, a marionette theatre performing fairy tales and folk tales from around the world with multicultural marionettes, cultural costume and music accompaniment. She taught puppetry in a Waldorf school in British Columbia, ran children's marionette troupes for Grades 4–6, and then began training other teachers internationally — traveling to early childhood conferences, libraries and schools as a trainer for decades before bringing all training online. Rudolf Steiner said that a young child who does puppet shows will not have the modern adolescent issues of pessimism, sarcasm and depression — Suzanne has dedicated her life's work to making this gift accessible to every parent and teacher.

🎓 Signature Training Programme:
• One-Year In-Depth Online Puppetry Training — the professional certificate programme. 31st group begins September 2026. Dives deep into the artistic, pedagogical and therapeutic aspects of puppetry for early childhood and all-age audiences. Covers puppet making, story writing, storytelling, staging, lighting, puppet movement and ensoulment. Content and assignments delivered monthly. Cost: $2,300 for the full year; payment plans always available. Limited places — register early. Email: suzannedown@gmail.com

📚 Shorter Courses & Mini Courses (Online):
• The Art and Joy of Lap Puppetry and the Instant Stage — 4-week beginner course. The "one-second stage" — magic with one puppet and one silk. Ideal for parents, teachers, grandparents. With bonus needle-felted table puppet course
• Introduction to the Rod Puppet — Pixie Puppet — skill-building; creating and enlivening a rod puppet
• Creating and Enlivening an Autumn Pixie Rod Puppet — 4-week seasonal course
• Silk Marionette Theater for Early Childhood — 6-week course; 40 years of marionette mastery now online
• Needle-Felted Puppet Stage Backdrops + Ocean Tale — creates gorgeous felt stages for any puppet work
• A Therapeutic Puppetry Toolbox — Nursery Rhyme Story Puppetry
• Shelter Stories in Puppetry — creating puppetry that helps children feel "all is well in the world"
• Busy Busy Bee — Early Childhood Puppetry Made Easy — mini course for all
• Dyeing Silk for Puppet Stages, Story Aprons and Nature Tables
• Walkabout Tales — Writing Stories Inspired by Walking in Nature
• A Year of Writing — writing seasonal stories, poetry and healing tales for children
• Start Your Own Puppet Tales Parent/Tot Programme — 8-week course on building a profitable puppetry business
• The Business of Puppetry — one-year action programme

☀️ Summer Professional Development Series — annual in-depth online Pro-D courses each summer. Multiple intensive courses offered July/August each year.

📖 Resources Developed: The Magical Story Apron (instant puppet theatre) · Rod Puppetry for Early Childhood · The Mother Archetype in Story · Nursery Rhyme Story and Puppetry for Language Development · Color and Light Puppetry · The Worker Character and Steiner's 12 Professions in Story · Puppetry for Birth to Three Years · Free monthly early childhood puppetry newsletter with free stories, articles and challenges

📱 Community: Facebook group "Waldorf Puppetry for Birth to Three Years" — resources and support for all students and graduates

Contact: suzanne@junipertreepuppets.com · suzannedown@gmail.com · Newsletter sign-up: junipertreepuppets.com

name: Puppetry in the Waldorf Curriculum — Why It Matters
detail: Puppetry is a core feature of Waldorf early childhood education. In kindergartens, the teacher tells stories through simple table or lap puppets — the child watches with open eyes and mouth, absorbing image and gesture without rational interference. Puppetry nourishes imagination, language, moral sense and the soul forces of the young child. The different puppet types are used at specific developmental stages: lap/table puppets for the very young (0–6), rod puppets for early grades, marionettes for Grades 4–6, hand puppets from Grade 2 onward.

name: ⭐ Christiaan Boele — Werbeck Singing / Healing Through Singing
detail: Finland (international). The foremost living practitioner of Werbeck singing — a therapeutic approach to the human voice developed by Valborg Werbeck-Svärdström and deeply connected to anthroposophy. Christiaan has been connected to Werbeck singing for over 50 years. He currently lives in Finland and conducts courses, schooling of the voice sessions, master classes and choirs around the world. Annual Healing Through Singing workshops at Marin Waldorf School, California (Healing Through Singing I, II, III — annually June). International workshops also in Europe. The Werbeck approach treats the voice not as an instrument to be trained but as a living expression of the whole human being — physical, soul and spiritual. Contact via BACWTT (bacwtt.org) for annual workshop registration.

Regular workshop presenter at WECAN conferences — connecting music and conscious movement for kindergarten teachers.

name: Nancy Blanning & Laurie Clark — Movement & Singing Games
detail: USA (Denver). Co-authors of Movement Journeys and Circle Adventures (Vols 1 & 2, WECAN). Laurie Clark co-author of Singing Games for Families, Schools and Communities (with Anna Rainville). International mentor and advisor to schools in Britain, Germany, Asia and Africa. Co-founder of Waldorf Modern Teacher Education UK. waldorfmodern.uk

name: ⭐ Sheila Phelps Johns — Lyre, Mood of the Fifth & International Music Training
detail: USA / International. BM (University of Southern California), MM (Wichita State University). Anthroposophic trainings in both instrumental and vocal music therapy. 14 years at Washington Waldorf School. Teaches Mood of the Fifth and pentatonic children's lyre for Grades 1–3, and applied music for Grades 7–8. Gives music courses in South America, China and internationally. Director of the Waldorf Music Teacher Training in China and the Philippines. President of the Lyre Association of North America for 12 years. Carrying member of AWME for 12+ years. Contact via waldorfmusic.org

name: ⭐ Andrea Lyman — AWME President & Waldorf Music Mentor
detail: USA / International. Bachelor's and Master's in vocal music education. Waldorf music teacher since 1992. Certified in Waldorf Music Education (Sunbridge College, 2005). Taught at Sunbridge College, West Coast Institute (BC, Canada) and Sound Circle Center. President of AWME. Organiser of the annual Waldorf Music Conference. Travels as music mentor to Waldorf schools throughout North America. Director of the Waldorf Music Teacher Training in China and the Philippines (jointly with Sheila Johns). Author of "Let There Be Music: The Music Curriculum in the Waldorf School Grades 1–8" — the most thorough free overview of the Waldorf music curriculum online. Contact: themusicpainter@gmail.com

name: ⭐ Sunbridge Institute — Elementary Music Teacher Education
detail: Chestnut Ridge, New York. 4-week certificate programme in Waldorf Elementary Music Teacher Education for Grades 1–8 music teachers. Coordinators: Jana Hawley and Adam Petersen. Curriculum: teaching music through the grades, chorus and recorder, music teachers seminar, child development, anthroposophy, inner development, meditative practice, and five days classroom observation with an experienced Waldorf music teacher. detail: USA / International. Professional organisation for lyre players and teachers in the Waldorf and anthroposophical tradition. Annual summer conference. Co-founded by Christof-Andreas Lindenberg — composer, music pioneer, living at Camphill School at Beaver Run, Pennsylvania, and still active at age 90. The lyre is introduced in Grade 1 in most Waldorf schools and is central to the music curriculum through early childhood. lyreassociation.org

detail: USA. Diploma in anthroposophic music therapy, Certified Music Practitioner, former Waldorf teacher. Faculty at Sophia's Hearth early childhood training and the Healing Education programme (M.Ed). Works in Waldorf schools, Camphill communities, hospice and therapeutic communities. centerforanthroposophy.org

name: Nordoff-Robbins Music Therapy — International ⭐
detail: Founded by Paul Nordoff (Waldorf teacher at Sunbridge) and Clive Robbins. Deeply rooted in Rudolf Steiner's anthroposophy. Based on the belief that everyone possesses a sensitivity to music that can be utilised for personal growth. Active music-making — improvisation, singing, composing — to support communication, self-expression and development. Training centres in UK, USA, Australia, Germany, New Zealand and South Africa. The most internationally established anthroposophically-rooted music therapy training in the world. nordoff-robbins.org.uk (UK) · nordoffrobbinscenternyc.org (USA)

detail: USA. Co-author (with Janet Langley) of The Roadmap to Literacy. Reading, phonics and literacy specialist for Waldorf Grades 1–3. Online workshops and resources. The most comprehensive guide to Waldorf-aligned literacy teaching currently available in English.

name: Torin Finser — Language Arts & Education
detail: USA. Author: School as a Journey (an eight-year Waldorf class teacher memoir); Silence Is Complicity; Organizational Integrity. Former Chair of Education Department at Antioch University New England. International lecturer. Faculty at Center for Anthroposophy. torinfinser.com

name: Waldorfish — Free Language Arts Resources
detail: Australia. Free Waldorf language arts worksheets, main lesson resources and curriculum ideas for homeschoolers and teachers. One of the most widely used free online Waldorf literacy resources. waldorfish.com

name: ⭐ Jennifer Militzer-Kopperl — Renewal of Literacy
detail: USA (California). Creator of the Renewal of Literacy® programme. Co-author (with Janet Langley) of The Roadmap to Literacy: Guide to Teaching Language Arts in Waldorf Schools Grades 1–3 (2018, 2022 Renewal Edition) and sole author of Continuing the Journey to Literacy: Grades 4–8 (2020). Together the two books form a complete Waldorf language arts curriculum for Grades 1–8. Combines linguistics, Lindamood-Bell remedial reading instruction and Waldorf pedagogy. Online workshops including "Tough, Bough, Cough and Dough: Meeting the Challenge of Teaching English" (free 2-hour intro video). renewalofliteracy.com · waldorfinspirations.com

name: Janet Langley — Waldorf Inspirations
detail: USA. Co-author of The Roadmap to Literacy (with Militzer-Kopperl). 40+ years Waldorf teaching. School mentor, evaluator and teacher training instructor. Co-creator of waldorfinspirations.com — free resource for Waldorf teachers with thousands of ideas for teaching Grades K–8. Workshop: "Teaching Literacy in Waldorf Grades 1–3." waldorfinspirations.com

name: Craig Giddens — Creative Speech
detail: USA (Maine/Seattle). Goetheanum-recognised speech artist since 1978. Waldorf class teacher, speech teacher and mentor in Waldorf schools in the USA and Europe for 50+ years. Founding member of the Center for Anthroposophy (NH) and the Speech School of North America. Faculty at Sound Circle Center (Seattle) and Waldorf High School Teacher Training (NH). Teaching speech at Maine Coast Waldorf School and mentoring Waldorf teachers. soundcirclecenter.org

name: Daniel Stokes — Storytelling & Drama
detail: USA (Portland). In the Waldorf Education movement since 1975. Trained at Emerson College, England. Co-founded Mythos Storytellers and Looking Glass Theater (Australia). 24+ years as Waldorf class teacher. Courses in poetry, storytelling and drama in Waldorf training centres throughout the USA. Spends part of each year abroad training teachers and mentoring in Waldorf schools. soundcirclecenter.org

name: The Nature Institute — Ryan Shea (Language Arts & Nature)
detail: USA (Ghent, New York). Research and education at the intersection of Waldorf education, Goethean science and living nature. Publications and workshops on language arts, science and the child's relationship to the living world. natureinstitute.org

name: The Nature Institute — Language & Nature
detail: Ghent, New York. Ryan Shea and colleagues. Workshop: "Seeing — Reading — Writing: Transforming Our Relationship to Language and Nature." Phenomenological approach to language and literacy through nature observation — deeply Goethean. natureinstitute.org

name: Craig Giddens — Creative Speech
detail: USA. Speech formation specialist and Waldorf educator. Creative Speech intensive workshops and speech therapy training aligned with the anthroposophical speech arts. Regular workshop presenter at Whatcom Hills Waldorf School, Bellingham WA and other Waldorf venues.

name: ⭐ Steiner School of Speech Arts — Chestnut Ridge, New York
detail:
Chestnut Ridge, New York (Threefold Community). The primary professional Creative Speech training in North America. 4-year full-time in-person training plus one-week intensive blocks open to any level. Three co-founders:

Helen Lubin — Founded "Speech Arts in Waldorf Schools in North America" (1994). Trained at Novalis School for Speech and Drama (Germany) and Goetheanum (Switzerland). Former instructor at School for Pedagogical and Therapeutic Speech, Dornach (1989–91) and Rudolf Steiner College (1992–2016). 250+ school speech visits to 60+ North American Waldorf schools. Therapeutic speech arts practitioner.
Barbara Renold — Co-founder. Trained at the Goetheanum and Harkness Studio (Sydney). Speech and drama teacher at Sunbridge College (1983–2007). Directed two complete cycles of Rudolf Steiner's four mystery dramas, culminating in the 2014 Threefold Mystery Drama Festival — the first time all four plays were presented by one cast in one conference in English.
Jennifer Kleinbach — Co-founder. Speech Formation diploma (Speech School of North America), Eurythmy diploma (Spring Valley). Teaches at School of Eurythmy, Sunbridge, Fiber Craft Studio. Performs with Eurythmy Spring Valley ensemble as speaker.

Contact: info@steinerspeecharts.org · steinerspeecharts.org

name: ⭐ Craig Giddens — Creative Speech (USA / International)
detail: USA (Freeport, Maine). Goetheanum-recognised speech artist since 1978. Waldorf class teacher, speech teacher and mentor for 50+ years in USA and Europe. Founding member of the Center for Anthroposophy (NH) and the Speech School of North America. Faculty at Sound Circle Center (Seattle) and Waldorf High School Teacher Training (NH). Currently mentoring teachers at Maine Coast Waldorf School. soundcirclecenter.org

name: Debra Spitulnik — Creative Speech (USA)
detail: USA. Creative Speech teacher for Washington Waldorf School, Center for Anthroposophy (NH) and the Waldorf Teacher Education Programme at Antioch University New England. Trained under Geoff Norris (Voicing the Silence). Faculty at Center for Anthroposophy. Essay: "Developing the Art of Imagination through Creative Speech" — one of the best introductions to Creative Speech for teachers. centerforanthroposophy.org

name: Christine Burke — Logodynamics & Creative Speech (USA)
detail: California, USA. Logodynamics Practitioner and Creative Speech Artist. Workshops at BACWTT (annual "Art of Speech" day) and internationally — for teachers, teacher trainees, actors, parents and business people. Travels to Waldorf schools, teacher trainings and Christian Communities worldwide. AASA member. bacwtt.org

name: ⭐ Artemis School of Speech and Drama (UK) — Christopher Garvey
detail: West Sussex, England. The primary Creative Speech and Drama training school in the UK. Formerly the Speech School. Christopher Garvey became Principal in 1990. Training in Speech Formation in the Steiner tradition. Garvey trained at Bristol Old Vic Drama School before completing Speech Formation training. The UK's longest-running Steiner-inspired speech training. speechanddrama.uk

name: Harkness Studio — Sydney, Australia (Mechthild Harkness)
detail: Sydney, Australia. The foremost Creative Speech training studio in Australasia. 4-year training: Year 1 epic poetry, Year 2 drama, Year 3 lyric poetry, Year 4 all three. Eurythmy, Greek gymnastics, performance and improvisation integral. Graduates have taught at the London School of Speech Formation and internationally (including China). Contact via Steiner Education Australia: steinereducation.edu.au

name: Geoff Norris — Voicing the Silence (International)
detail: International. Developing the "Archetype Technique" — a modular professional training deeply grounded in anthroposophy. Renewing the impulse of Rudolf and Marie Steiner alongside Michael Chekhov, Viola Spolin and Rudolf Laban. Goetheanum-recognised speech diploma available. An "Alchemical Theatre of Transformation — a Theatre of the Future." speechanddramastudio.com

name: Séamus Maynard — EduCareDo Speech & Drama (Online)
detail: International (online). Speech and Drama as Living Arts — a year-long online foundation course inspired by Rudolf Steiner and Michael Chekhov. Monthly embodied and experiential exercises. Open to Waldorf teachers, artists and anyone deepening their artistic practice. Trained at Guildhall (London), studied Michael Chekhov Technique, co-founded Shakespeare Alive!, studied speech formation with Christy MacKaye Barnes and Christopher Garvey (Artemis). educaredo.org

name: Dawn Langman — Speech Formation (Australia)
detail: Australia. Speech Formation artist working to bridge speech formation with Michael Chekhov's acting methodology. Referenced internationally as a leading developer at the intersection of Steiner speech arts and contemporary performance. Contact via Steiner Education Australia.

name: Association for Anthroposophic Speech Arts (AASA)
detail: USA / International. Professional association for speech artists trained in the anthroposophic tradition. Member directory, articles, professional development. Members include Helen Lubin, Christine Burke, Kim Snyder-Vine, Diane Caracciolo, Anja Macmurchie and many others. creativespeech.org

name: ⭐ Eurythmy Spring Valley — School of Eurythmy
detail: Chestnut Ridge, New York (Threefold Community). 4-year full-time professional eurythmy training. New first-year class forming (New Frontier Part-time Class also forming). Graduates go on to teach in Waldorf schools, perform as stage artists or practice as therapeutic eurythmists. Part of the Threefold Community alongside Sunbridge, Green Meadow Waldorf School. eurythmy.org

name: ⭐ Sound Circle Eurythmy Training (SCE)
detail: Pacific Northwest, USA. 4-year part-time eurythmy training led by master teachers David-Michael Monasch and Glenda Monasch (both Goetheanum graduates). Overseen by Shaina Stoehr of the West Midlands Eurythmy Training (UK). The only English-language eurythmy training with rigorous comparative movement studies context. Summer trips to Europe (Goetheanum + Greece/Renaissance centres). soundcircleeurythmy.org

name: Goetheanum — School of Spiritual Science: Eurythmy Section
detail: Dornach, Switzerland. The world headquarters for eurythmy training and research. Academy for Eurythmic Art. Annual graduation programmes attended by eurythmy schools worldwide. Also: annual Eurythmy Summer Intensive weeks open to students and professionals. goetheanum.org

name: EANA — Eurythmy Association of North America
detail: USA / Canada. Voluntary association of eurythmists on the North American continent. Annual conference (October — Keene, NH 2025). Workshops: Eurythmy in the Working Life (led by Leonore Russell). eana.org · Contact: leonorerussell@gmail.com

name: Eurythmy Association Australia/NZ (ETANZA)
detail: Australia / New Zealand. Professional association of eurythmists in Australia and New Zealand. Workshops, training support, practitioner directory. The primary eurythmy professional body for the Southern Hemisphere. Contact via Anthroposophical Society Australia.

name: Leonore Russell — Eurythmy in the Working Life
detail: USA. Practitioner of social eurythmy — "Eurythmy in the Working Life" — for adults, businesses and Waldorf school faculties. Trained with Anne Marie Ehrlich. 25+ years practice. Annual workshops at Center for Anthroposophy (Keene/Wilton NH). Contact: leonorerussell@gmail.com

name: West Midlands Eurythmy Training (UK)
detail: United Kingdom. Shaina Stoehr, director. Under the aegis of the School of Spiritual Science at the Goetheanum. Part-time professional eurythmy training in the UK. Oversees Sound Circle Eurythmy Training (USA). British Council for Eurythmy also maintains practitioner listings for the UK.

name: Barbara Bresette-Mills — Online Eurythmy
detail: USA / Online. Regular online eurythmy workshops and webinars for the broader Waldorf community — "Soul Warmth and Light in Winter," seasonal eurythmy webinars. Contact via Anthroposophical Society in America (anthroposophy.org).

name: ⭐ Eurythmy Spring Valley — 4-year Full-Time Training
detail: Chestnut Ridge, New York (Threefold Community). The flagship North American eurythmy training. Led by David-Michael Monasch and Glenda Monasch (both graduates of the Academy for Eurythmic Art at the Goetheanum, Switzerland). 4-year full-time professional training — graduates become Waldorf school teachers, therapeutic eurythmy practitioners and stage artists. Annual summer intensives also open to non-degree students. Overseen by Shaina Stoehr (West Midlands Eurythmy Training UK) under the School of Spiritual Science, Goetheanum. eurythmy.org

name: ⭐ Sound Circle Eurythmy Training (SCE) — Boulder, Colorado
detail: Boulder, Colorado, USA. 4-year part-time eurythmy training — unique focus on comparative movement studies and Waldorf pedagogy grounding. Led by David-Michael and Glenda Monasch. Under the aegis of the School of Spiritual Science at the Goetheanum, overseen by Shaina Stoehr (West Midlands UK). Students make two summer study trips to Europe including the Goetheanum. soundcircleeurythmy.org

name: Kleber Akama — Eurythmy (Brazil)
detail: Brazil. Eurythmist working in South America. Presented at the 2025 Festival and Exploration of Eurythmy in Waldorf Education alongside high school students from both North and South America. One of the leading eurythmy educators in Latin America. Contact via Brazilian Waldorf schools or FEWB.

name: ⭐ Waldorf Handwork Educators (WHE) — Elizabeth Seward PhD & Shellie Smith
detail: USA / International (Online). Founded 2013. Two-Year Online International Handwork Teacher Development Programme — 225+ hours live instruction, 190–240 hours hands-on projects, 50–100 hours reading/reflection, classroom observation and practice teaching, monthly assignments, mentoring, Grades K–8 portfolio. Cohort participants come from all four corners of the earth. Now enrolling August 2026. Also: annual international conference (Deep Roots, Strong Branches — July 2025) for all Waldorf subject teachers. Curriculum guides, video resources, skills classes. waldorfhandwork.org

name: ⭐ Fiber Craft Studio — Applied Arts Programme
detail: Chestnut Ridge, New York (Threefold Community). Founded by Chris Marlow (Co-Director, 2012–present). 4-year part-time professional handwork teacher training. Meets two weeks each summer + one week each winter. Covers handwork Grades 1–8 (two grades per year), arts (painting, drawing, form drawing, geometric drawing, sculpture), eurythmy, Spacial Dynamics, speech work. Full-time Mon–Fri during sessions. Located on the Threefold Community campus beside Sunbridge Institute and Green Meadow Waldorf School. fibercraftstudio.org

name: ⭐ Waldorf Practical Arts Training (WPAT) — Waldorf Institute of Southern California
detail: California, USA (+ Online). AWSNA-accredited certification programme. 9 × six-day intensive modules over 3 years. Fibre arts, woodworking, metalworking, stone carving throughout the grades and their connection to child development and the curriculum. Flexible enrolment — modules do not have to be taken in order. In-person at Waldorf School of Orange County. Faculty: Ania Kubik (20 years handwork), Jodie Jean Marston-Arellano (handwork + music). waldorfteaching.org

name: ⭐ Chenoa Pelligra — Peace with Nature Handwork
detail: USA (travelling internationally). 18+ years. Seasonal nature crafts, knitting, felting, weaving. Ages 5–adults. 65K Instagram followers @peacewithnaturehandwork. Online courses and in-person workshops. peacewithnaturehandwork.com

name: Betsan Corkhill — Knitting for Health & Wellness
detail: UK. Author of Knit for Health and Wellness — research-based exploration of knitting's measurable physical and mental health benefits. Used in Waldorf handwork teacher education conferences (WHE). knitforlife.com

name: Handwork 2026 International Conference
detail: International online conference for Waldorf handwork teachers and educators. Presented by WHE and partner organisations. Annual July gathering. handwork2026.org

name: Meg Quinlisk — Handwork (Australia)
detail: Australia. Steiner early childhood settings specialist. Graduate of WHE Handwork Teacher Development Programme. Teaches in Sydney Rudolf Steiner College early childhood teacher training — specialising in festivals, puppetry, dollmaking, storytelling and biography work. The primary handwork-connected early childhood specialist in Australia's Waldorf teacher training.

name: ⭐ WHE Annual Conferences — Three per Year (International)
detail: Waldorf Handwork Educators runs three international online conferences each year: February (therapeutic/community handwork — Feb 15–17, 2025: "Power of Community Handwork"; faculty Betsan Corkhill, Brecia Kralovic-Logan, Sven Saar); July (all Waldorf subject teachers — July 2025: "Collaboration is the Heart," includes music, world languages, handwork, woodwork teachers); August (Teaching Handwork Grades 1–8 — four weekly sessions, timed for USA/Australia/Philippines/SE Asia). All conferences online, recorded, financial aid available. waldorfhandwork.org

name: Kelly Beekman — Hand Held Arts
detail: USA. Artist and educator with 20+ years teaching experience. Waldorf class teacher, mentor, workshop leader and tutor. Online courses for teachers, parents and artists. B.A. fine art (Bowdoin College), M.Ed Waldorf Education (Antioch University New England), art education certification (School of Visual Arts NYC). Conference faculty at WHE. handheldarts.com

name: Sven Saar — International Handwork & Waldorf Mentoring (UK)
detail: UK (and international). 30+ years teaching experience in Germany and England. 8 years as Waldorf class teacher in England, specialising in history and drama. Full-time in teacher education — faculty of several UK and international Waldorf courses and universities. International lecturer and active mentor and advisor to schools in Britain, Germany, Asia and Africa. Co-founder of Waldorf Modern Teacher Education UK. Conference keynote at WHE February 2024. waldorfmodern.uk

name: Brecia Kralovic-Logan — Spiral of Creativity
detail: USA. Champion for women's voices and nationally recognised fiber artist. Author of The Spiral of Creativity: Mastering the Art of a Spirited Life. Conference faculty at WHE February 2025. Explores the creative process through fiber arts and the Waldorf tradition.

name: ⭐ Jamie York — Making Math Meaningful
detail: USA (Denver/Boulder). 30+ years Waldorf mathematics teaching. Taught middle school and high school maths at Shining Mountain Waldorf School, Boulder for 21 years. Now a "maths missionary" — travels across USA and internationally offering workshops for teachers to re-imagine mathematics. Author of the definitive Waldorf maths curriculum series: Making Math Meaningful (Grades 1–5, 6–8, High School). Online grade-specific workshops (Grades 1–12, 8+ hours video each) and Re-Imagining Mathematics Workshops (5 hours). Online homeschool academy for Waldorf-based maths, science and humanities (Grades 6–12). jamieyorkacademy.com · jamieyork.com

name: ⭐ Nettie Fabrie — Remedial Mathematics & Teacher Training
detail: Netherlands / USA (Seattle). 40-year teaching career beginning in Dutch public schools, then Waldorf class teacher taking two classes from Grades 1–8 in Holland. Former pedagogical director at Seattle Waldorf School (2001–2018). Co-author of Making Math Meaningful: Grades 1–5 (with Wim Gottenbos and Jamie York). Founded a Waldorf teacher training programme in the Czech Republic. Core faculty and grade school teacher training director at Sound Circle Center, Seattle. AWSNA Teacher Education Delegates Circle. Remedial specialist mentoring teachers in Netherlands, Czech Republic and USA. Retired 2025, now on the island of Öland, Sweden.

name: Wim Gottenbos — Remedial Specialist & Mentor
detail: Netherlands / USA (Seattle). Taught in Dutch public schools 12 years before becoming a Waldorf teacher. Three classes from Grades 1–8 at Seattle Waldorf School. Co-author of Making Math Meaningful: Grades 1–5 (with Nettie Fabrie and Jamie York). Since 2017: mentor and evaluator for Waldorf schools in the Pacific Northwest. Remedial specialist bridging maths learning difficulties with Waldorf methodology.

name: Waldorf Math with Mariam
detail: UK. Trained Waldorf and state teacher. Mathematics specialist for Waldorf homeschoolers. Online resources, mentoring, curriculum support. Instagram: @waldorfwithmariam · waldorfwithmariam.com

name: Lotus & Ivy Education
detail: Online. Waldorf-aligned mathematics resources and curriculum support for homeschoolers. Grades 1–8. Beautiful, developmentally appropriate worksheets and block books.

name: Justin Howard — Waldorf High School Mathematics
detail: USA. Upper grades math teacher at Detroit Waldorf School. Co-director (with Rebecca Howard) of Sunbridge Institute Elementary Programme from 2025. Faculty Sunbridge Institute. Specialises in middle and upper school Waldorf mathematics pedagogy.

name: Ernst Schuberth — Mathematics Curriculum (Germany)
detail: Germany. Author of the Waldorf mathematics curriculum texts — Form Drawing 1st to 4th Grade and Mathematics for the Waldorf School. Available in German via Rudolf Steiner Verlag; in English via Waldorf Publications. The foundational academic mathematical pedagogy resource.

name: ⭐ Center for Anthroposophy — Mentor Training Programme
detail: Wilton/Keene, New Hampshire, USA (+ online). "Wisdom into Practice: Pedagogical Leadership for Waldorf Teachers." Certificate-earning advanced training — comprehensive preparation in pedagogical mentoring, coaching and professional evaluation. Meets once monthly online for ten months + week-long in-person summer residency. Prepares experienced educators to mentor and evaluate developing Waldorf teachers across a wide network of schools. Enrollment opens October 2025 for 2026 cohort. Contact: karen@centerforanthroposophy.org · centerforanthroposophy.org

name: ⭐ AWSNA Mentor Training in Partnership
detail: USA / International. AWSNA's Pedagogical Mentoring in Partnership project — preparing seasoned teachers to become pedagogical mentors working in collaboration with new and developing teachers. Certificate programme. Contact via waldorfeducation.org

name: Sunbridge Institute — Elementary Teacher Education
detail: Chestnut Ridge, New York. Low-residency and online Waldorf teacher education. Elementary (Grades 1–8), Early Childhood, and High School certificate programmes. Faculty: Nancy Blanning (EC co-director), Rebecca & Justin Howard (Elementary co-directors), Brigida Ashworth (eurythmy). Continuing education and Summer Series for working teachers. sunbridge.edu

name: WECAN Annual Conference — Professional Development
detail: USA / Online. Annual February early childhood educators' conference. 2025 faculty included: Laurie Clark (singing games), Nancy Blanning (developmental movement), Leslie Wetzonis Woolverton (IDEA coordinator, mentor), Patricia Regan (eurythmy and music), Ruth Ker (WECAN board, child development). Online recordings available through April after each conference. waldorfearlychildhood.org

name: Alliance for Public Waldorf — Summer Professional Development
detail: USA / Online. Annual summer virtual professional development specifically for the Public Waldorf community. Available to all Waldorf educators. allianceforpublicwaldorf.org

name: Waldorf High School Teacher Education Programme
detail: Wilton, NH and Online (Center for Anthroposophy). For high school teachers preparing to educate adolescents in sciences, humanities or arts. Low-residency + online. Three summer intensives + independent studies, mentored research and internship. For educators already teaching full-time. Earn a graduate-level certificate. centerforanthroposophy.org

name: Waldorf Teacher Rejuvenation Courses (BACWTT)
detail: San Francisco Bay Area, California (+ online). Annual June/July rejuvenation courses for working Waldorf teachers: Early Childhood Teacher Rejuvenation · Grades 1–5 Rejuvenation (Finding Gold) · Grades 6–8 Rejuvenation. bacwtt.org

name: International Campus Waldorf (ICW)
detail: International. Online learning platform for Waldorf teachers worldwide. Connects teachers across institutions — Freie Hochschule Stuttgart, Sunbridge, Sound Circle, BACWTT, Waldorf Teacher Institute and others. E-learning resources, courses and international connections. international-campus-waldorf.com

name: ⭐ Waldorf-Ideen-Pool (Germany)
detail: waldorf-ideen-pool.de · Founded and run by Marcus Kraneburg. "The Waldorf movement lives from an incredible productivity. The Waldorf-Ideen-Pool wants to capture and reflect a breath of that." Probably the largest free material and ideas collection of the Waldorf movement in the world. An ideas treasure trove (Ideen-Fundgrube) for teachers and educators across all subjects and all grades. Student work examples, lesson ideas, pedagogical suggestions, job listings, continuing education and products from the Waldorf world. Primarily in German. Browse or search freely — viel Freude beim Stöbern! (Great joy in browsing!)

name: E-Learning Waldorf — Elewa (Germany)
detail: Germany. Online continuing education platform for Waldorf teachers. Professional development courses and modules in German. elewa.de

name: ECSWE — European Council for Steiner Waldorf Education
detail: Brussels, Belgium. The European umbrella body for national Steiner Waldorf associations across 34 countries. Policy, research, international dialogue on quality standards. ecswe.eu

name: Freie Hochschule Stuttgart (Germany)
detail: The original Waldorf teacher training institute, founded 1946 beside the first Waldorf school in Stuttgart. Bachelor and Master programmes in Waldorf education. The academic heartland of the movement. freie-hochschule-stuttgart.de

name: Waldorf International — Hague Circle
detail: International Conference of Waldorf Pedagogy. Educators from all continents meet twice yearly at the Goetheanum or in member countries. International coordination and pedagogical dialogue. waldorf-international.org

name: Erziehungskunst (Germany)
detail: The journal for parents, teachers and all interested in Waldorf education. Articles, curriculum discussions, festivals, school life. Published by the Bund der Freien Waldorfschulen. Also available as app. erziehungskunst.de

name: Kim John Payne MEd
detail: Australia/USA. Simplicity Parenting; The Soul of Discipline; The Games Children Play; Waldorf Games Handbook. Speaks to 10,000–20,000 parents/teachers/year internationally. Waldorf Collaborative Counseling Program director at Antioch. Social Inclusion Approach implemented in 200+ schools worldwide. simplicitypare nting.com

name: Jean Miller — Art of Homeschooling
detail: USA. 25+ years Waldorf homeschooling mentor. Podcast. Inspired at Home membership community (monthly masterclasses + coaching calls). artofhomeschooling.com

name: Melisa & Erik Nielsen — Waldorf Essentials
detail: USA. Grades K–8 curriculum with mentoring included. Podcast. 20.3K Instagram. waldorfessentials.com

name: ⭐ Sophie — Waldorf This Way
detail:
New Zealand. Experienced Waldorf class teacher, curriculum developer and passionate advocate for bringing Waldorf education into the 21st century — blending Steiner's original indications with modern educational research. Instagram: @waldorfthisway · "Reimagining Steiner education for today's children, schools and world."

🎓 What Sophie offers:
• Waldorf Your Way — personalised 1:1 homeschool curriculum planning programme. Four comprehensive modules moving from overwhelm to confident, personalised Waldorf curriculum. Covers year overview, main lesson block planning, practice blocks, subject-specific planning (form drawing, wet-on-wet painting, handwork, movement). Regular 60-minute 1:1 calls + ongoing feedback throughout. Designed for homeschoolers; can be adapted for classroom teachers.
• Main Lesson Block Curriculum Guides — comprehensive 3–6 week daily teaching guides for core lower school main lessons. Include review, new learning, bookwork, stories, morning circle activities and assessment. Available via her Etsy shop.
• Teaching & Planning Resources — affordable templates, tools and resources for curriculum planning and teaching.
• Starpath Learning — full open-and-go Waldorf-inspired homeschool curriculum via monthly subscription. Every step of the day provided. Beautiful web platform with tailor-made curriculum, progress tracking and year planning. starpathlearning.com
• Personalised 1:1 coaching calls — individual sessions for ongoing mentoring and support throughout the school year. Also supports diverse learners (ADHD, dyslexia and other learning challenges).

Contact: hello@waldorfthisway.com · waldorfthisway.com · Instagram: @waldorfthisway · Etsy: etsy.com/nz/shop/Waldorfthisway

name: Waldorf Teacher Resources
detail: Free online resource portal organised by grade and subject. Math, language arts, science, history, arts — extensive free materials for teachers and homeschoolers. waldorfteacherresources.com

name: Waldorf Teacher Institute
detail: USA. Teacher preparation programs for Early Childhood and Grades 1–8. Integrates conceptual study, artistic engagement, practical experiences, student initiatives and faculty mentoring. waldorfteachertraining.org

name: Patti Connolly (Student Support / Remedial)
detail: USA. 30+ years; class teacher, remedial specialist, pedagogical director, mentor, evaluator. Mentors Kindergarten–4th Grade teachers. Student Support Teacher at Waldorf School of the Roaring Fork, Colorado. waldorfinspirations.com

name: Susan Perrow
detail: Australia. Therapeutic storytelling specialist. Healing Stories for Challenging Behaviour; Therapeutic Storytelling; An A–Z Collection of Behaviour Tales. Internationally trains teachers and therapists in story medicine. Hawthorn Press.

name: Henning Köhler
detail: Germany. Working with Anxious, Nervous and Depressed Children. Curative educator and anthroposophical psychotherapist. Practical guidance on supporting emotionally struggling children. Translated into many languages.

name: ⭐ Robyn M. Brown — The Mulberry Centre for Curative Education
detail: USA (Gold Beach, Oregon). 33+ years as a Waldorf teacher. After teaching a full grades cycle, apprenticed in curative education with Sunny Baldwin at Somerset School (the landmark programme where "children who came got better — healing happened"). Founded Mulberry Classroom in 2001 (San Francisco, later Santa Rosa, now at Poppy Hill Center). Author of A Practical Guide to Curative Education: The Ladder of the Seven Life Processes (Lindisfarne Books / SteinerBooks, 440 pages) — "At a time when experienced educators are struck by how classroom dynamics have changed, this is a much-needed reminder of a tried-and-tested approach that can work for every child." Faculty at BACWTT (Bay Area Center for Waldorf Teacher Training) and Center for Anthroposophy (Wilton NH). Offers: 3-year Curative Education Training Program (Year 1 foundation; Year 2 $3,500; Year 3 $1,750); mentoring for teachers and schools worldwide; workshops; newer course "Practical Applications of Anthroposophical Education." Her training covers: the six curative polarities, twelve senses, seven life processes, and Steiner's original curative education lectures. Her philosophy: "Rudolf Steiner's wish was that every teacher be a curative teacher, and that every child would have a place in a Waldorf school."

name: ⭐ Michaelann Murphy — Earth & Sky Farm Community (USA)
detail: Wilton, New Hampshire, USA. Biodynamic farmer, Waldorf educator and founder of Earth and Sky Farm Community. Master's degree in Waldorf Education. Teaching certification encompasses early childhood through high school. Experienced educator — has taught nursery, kindergarten and grades children in a number of Waldorf and private schools. Prior director of several early childhood centres and farm-based education programmes. Served in Waldorf schools as pedagogical chair, governance group member and early education mentor. Has long held educational circles and studies for adults in community — through movement, parent education, therapeutic agricultural activities and teacher enrichment. Passionate about creating and guiding programmes for the healing of the earth and the therapeutic effects of agriculture and nature in both children and adults. Faculty at the Center for Anthroposophy (Wilton NH) summer renewal programme. earthandskyfarm.org · centerforanthroposophy.org

name: Beatrice Pintado — Waldorf Mentor (Mexico)
detail: Mexico. Waldorf educator and mentor working with parents and children in the Mexican Waldorf community. Contact via the Mexican Waldorf school network or through local Waldorf school associations for current programmes and availability.

name: Kim John Payne MEd — Simplicity Parenting (Australia / USA / International)
detail: Australia/USA. Simplicity Parenting — the most widely read Waldorf-adjacent parenting book worldwide. Director of the Waldorf Collaborative Counseling Programme at Antioch University New England. Social Inclusion Approach implemented in 200+ schools. Speaks to 10,000–20,000 parents and teachers per year internationally. Books: Simplicity Parenting · The Soul of Discipline · The Games Children Play. simplicityparenting.com

name: Susan Perrow — Therapeutic Storytelling (Australia / International)
detail: Australia. Therapeutic storytelling for children's behavioural and emotional challenges. Books: Healing Stories for Challenging Behaviour · Therapeutic Storytelling · An A–Z Collection of Behaviour Tales. Internationally trains teachers and therapists in story medicine. Hawthorn Press. susanperrow.com

name: Henning Köhler — Child Psychology (Germany / International)
detail: Germany. Curative educator and anthroposophical psychotherapist. Author of Working with Anxious, Nervous and Depressed Children — one of the most cited anthroposophical books on child psychology. name: ⭐ 1. You Are Your Child's First Teacher — Rahima Baldwin Dancy
detail: Hawthorn Press / Ten Speed Press. The single most recommended first book for Waldorf parents worldwide. The first book in America to popularise Rudolf Steiner's insights regarding the developmental needs of young children. Covers birth to age 6: language and cognitive development, appropriate toys, nourishing artistic abilities, discipline, early childhood programmes, toilet training and using home life as curriculum. Today's society pressures us into overstimulating young children — Dancy speaks up for a rational approach that helps children be children. "If you are just going to get one book as an introduction to Waldorf parenting — this is the one." Revised edition with updated resources. Rating: 4.01/5 from 1,837 readers on Goodreads. name: ⭐ 2. Beyond the Rainbow Bridge — Barbara J. Patterson & Pamela Bradley
detail: Michaelmas Press. The ideal companion to You Are Your Child's First Teacher. A wonderful starting place for understanding the Waldorf approach to the early years — gentle parenting through rhythm, simple toys, less haste and respectful presence. Patterson draws on years of parent-child class groups with honest questions from parents and practical suggestions. Covers birth through age seven. Explains the "rainbow bridge" — the passage from the spiritual world into earthly life — with warmth and clarity. Rating: 4.01/5 from 679 readers. Michaelmas Press.

detail: Ballantine Books. The most widely read Waldorf-adjacent parenting book of the last 20 years — and not just in Waldorf circles. Based on Payne's work with thousands of families. Not explicitly Waldorf but shares all the same values. Rating: 4.22/5 from 16,000+ readers. A book that genuinely changes family life. Grounded, warm and deeply applicable. Covers daily, weekly and seasonal rhythms, the Waldorf approach to play, story, art and nature. Rating: 4.34/5 from 686 readers — exceptionally highly rated. name: 5. Free to Learn — Lynne Oldfield
detail: Hawthorn Press. A clear, warm guide to the principles and methods of Waldorf early childhood education — drawing on kindergarten experience from around the world. Stories, helpful insights, observations and photographs. Explains what lies behind the Waldorf kindergarten — imitation, reverence, rhythm, play, the artistic environment — without being academic. An excellent bridge between the philosophical and the practical. Hawthorn Press.

Highly recommended for parents of school-age children wanting to understand what their child is doing and why. Rating: 3.75/5 from 651 readers. Gryphon House.

Parents considering Waldorf find enormous comfort here: the dedication, creativity and warmth of Waldorf teaching made vivid and human. Illustrates the remarkable relationship between teacher, student, family and school community across eight years. Rating: widely loved. Essential reading for any Waldorf parent. detail: Michaelmas Press. One of the most complete family reference guides. Michaelmas Press.

A practical, compassionate and insightful guide for parents and teachers of adolescents — covering the developmental tasks of the high school years, social life, sexuality, identity and the relationship between parents and teenagers. Betty Staley is one of the most respected voices in Waldorf high school education. Hawthorn Press.

Available in English and Spanish (Editorial Rudolf Steiner). One of the most cited child psychology books in Waldorf education. SteinerBooks.

name: ⭐ The Education of the Child (GA 34) — Rudolf Steiner
detail: SteinerBooks / Anthroposophic Press. The foundational short essay — read this first of all Steiner's education texts. The most complete account of child development, the threefold human being and the psychology of education. Not easy — but of inexhaustible depth. Read slowly, repeatedly, in a study group. name: ⭐ The Kingdom of Childhood (GA 311) — Rudolf Steiner
detail: SteinerBooks. Seven lectures given in Torquay, England, August 1924 — Steiner's last series of education lectures before his death. An ideal second Steiner education text. SteinerBooks / Rudolf Steiner Press.

name: ⭐ Waldorf Education: Ideas of Rudolf Steiner in Practice — Christopher Clouder & Martyn Rawson
detail: Floris Books. The most comprehensive modern overview of the complete Waldorf curriculum K–12 by two of the most respected British Waldorf educators. Covers every subject area, the developmental stages, the school as a social organism, teacher development and assessment. Essential reading for any teacher entering the Waldorf profession. name: ⭐ Waldorf Education: A Human Approach (Education Towards Freedom) — Frans Carlgren
detail: Floris Books / Rudolf Steiner Schools Fellowship. A survey of Waldorf schools worldwide with hundreds of photographs. One of the most visually rich introductions to Waldorf education — showing real school life across many countries and grades. A book that has introduced more teachers to Waldorf than almost any other. Floris Books.

name: Phases of Childhood — Bernard Lievegoed
detail: Floris Books. The essential developmental guide for Waldorf teachers. Belgian psychiatrist and anthroposophist Bernard Lievegoed describes the three major developmental phases of childhood in exquisite detail — the dreaming phase (0–7), the imaginative phase (7–14) and the thinking phase (14–21) — and their implications for education. One of the most widely read books in Waldorf teacher education worldwide. Floris Books.

name: Lighting Fires: Deepening Education Through Meditation — Jørgen Smit

detail: WECAN. Compiled articles on the development of the young child, the Waldorf approach to the first three years, imitation and the body, rhythm and the environment. Essential reading for parents and carers of very young children in a Waldorf context. WECAN Books.

detail: SteinerBooks. Short, profound meditations on education and child development for daily contemplation. A beloved companion for Waldorf parents and teachers. SteinerBooks.

name: The Genius of Play — Sally Jenkinson
detail: Hawthorn Press. The definitive book on Waldorf play. Celebrates the spirit of childhood play — free, unstructured, imaginative play — and makes the case for protecting it in a world that increasingly undervalues it. Essential reading for any parent or early childhood educator. Hawthorn Press.

name: ⭐ The Philosophy of Freedom / Intuitive Thinking as a Spiritual Path (GA 4) — Rudolf Steiner
detail:
Rudolf Steiner, 1894. The philosophical cornerstone of everything Steiner ever said or did. Steiner's clearest and most demanding statement of epistemology, moral autonomy and the method of intuitive thinking. Argues that true human freedom lies not in the absence of external constraint but in the capacity to act from pure thinking — from love for the deed itself, with no other motive. The book that establishes Steiner's credentials as a serious philosopher before anthroposophy properly begins.

"What I want to present in this book is a science of freedom. To resolve all other questions and riddles is not the primary task of philosophy — that task is to establish the foundations of all other knowledge."

Why Waldorf teachers should read it: Every element of Waldorf pedagogy — the freedom to teach from living understanding rather than fixed methods, the respect for each child's individuality, the refusal to indoctrinate — flows from this book's philosophical foundation. The Waldorf teacher who has truly understood the Philosophy of Freedom teaches from freedom. The teacher who has not yet read it may still teach beautifully — but will not understand why.

Recommended translation: Michael Wilson (Rudolf Steiner Press) is widely preferred. Also: "Intuitive Thinking as a Spiritual Path" (Anthroposophic Press, trans. Michael Lipson) — same text, excellent translation. Available free at rsarchive.org.

name: ⭐ Theosophy: An Introduction to the Spiritual Processes in Human Life and in the Cosmos (GA 9) — Rudolf Steiner
detail:
Rudolf Steiner, 1904. The most accessible entry point into Steiner's complete worldview. Introduces the fourfold human being — physical body, life body (etheric), soul body (astral) and ego — as well as the soul members and spirit members. Covers reincarnation, karma and the soul's journey between death and rebirth. Short (under 200 pages), clear and beautifully structured. Despite the potentially off-putting title — "Theosophy" — this is not Blavatsky's Theosophy but Steiner's own spiritual science, using the same vocabulary in his own way.

Why Waldorf teachers and parents should read it: The threefold human being underpins all of Waldorf education — the three-seven year developmental stages, the relationship between thinking, feeling and willing, the education of head, heart and hands. Theosophy is where you learn what the threefold human being actually is in Steiner's own words. Rating: 4.12/5 from 791 readers on Goodreads. Available free at rsarchive.org.

name: ⭐ How to Know Higher Worlds / Knowledge of the Higher Worlds (GA 10) — Rudolf Steiner
detail:
Rudolf Steiner, 1904. Steiner's fundamental handbook for inner development. A precise, practical manual of exercises and stages for developing spiritual perception — with careful attention to psychological safety, grounding and balance. More than 100 years after first publication, it remains — alongside meditation, channelling, remote viewing and astral projection — uniquely precise in its instructions for inner training, protective exercises and grounding.

Why Waldorf teachers should read it: Steiner insisted that the Waldorf teacher's inner development — their capacity for genuine reverence, wonder and self-knowledge — is at least as important as their pedagogical skill. This book is the guide to that inner work. Rating: 4.21/5 from 1,947 readers. The most widely read Steiner book worldwide. Available free at rsarchive.org.

name: ⭐ An Outline of Esoteric Science (Occult Science — An Outline) (GA 13) — Rudolf Steiner
detail:
Rudolf Steiner, 1910. Of all Steiner's books, this one perhaps comes closest to containing the whole of his spiritual teaching in one volume. Systematic presentation of the constitution of the human being, the evolution of the earth and humanity through the great cosmic stages (Saturn, Sun, Moon, Earth, Jupiter, Venus, Vulcan), reincarnation and karma in depth, and the complete path of initiation. Dense, demanding — and inexhaustibly deep.

"Given his energetic involvement in practical initiatives and extensive lecturing, Steiner had very little time to write books. Of those he did write, four titles form an indispensable introduction to his later teaching: Knowledge of the Higher Worlds, Occult Science, The Philosophy of Freedom and Theosophy."

Read slowly. Read with a study group if possible. Do not expect to understand it on first reading — each re-reading over years reveals new dimensions. Available free at rsarchive.org. SteinerBooks edition recommended. Rating: 4.23/5.

name: The Foundation Stone Meditation — Rudolf Steiner (Christmas Conference 1923)
detail: The spiritual cornerstone of the re-founded Anthroposophical Society — given by Steiner at the Christmas Conference in Dornach, December 1923. A meditation verse in four movements, one for each season, encompassing the whole of anthroposophy in concentrated poetic form. Often described as the most complete spiritual verse Steiner ever gave. Read slowly, meditatively, alongside a commentary — many good ones available (Sergei Prokofieff, Florin Lowndes). A book of great depth and beauty. Available free at rsarchive.org. Rudolf Steiner Press / SteinerBooks.

name: ⭐ 1. Giving Love, Bringing Joy — Hand Gesture Games and Lullabies in the Mood of the Fifth
detail: Wilma Ellersiek. Translated by Lyn and Kundry Willwerth. WECAN Books, 2003. The foundational book — start here. Gentle, loving games and songs incorporating the healing, enlivening qualities of gesture, touch and movement. Designed for the very youngest children — from birth through the early years. Songs in the Mood of the Fifth. Touch games between parent and baby. Lullabies and hand games for lying-down play. "These games and lullabies are imbued with the idea that loving contact with children helps them establish a nurturing relation with plants, animals, people and things." Companion CD available separately. ISBN 978-0-9796232-6-4

name: ⭐ 2. Gesture Games for Autumn and Winter
detail: Wilma Ellersiek. Translated by Lyn and Kundry Willwerth. WECAN Books. Seasonal gesture games, fingerplays and songs in the Mood of the Fifth for kindergarten and lower grades. Autumn and winter nature themes. 32 songs and gesture games. Margret Costanini's introduction outlines the educational basis of example and imitation. Companion CD available. ISBN 978-0-9722238-9-8

name: ⭐ 3. Gesture Games for Spring and Summer
detail: Wilma Ellersiek. Translated by Lyn and Kundry Willwerth. WECAN Books, 2005. 32 songs and gesture games inspired by spring and summer nature. Craft directions and a biography of Ellersiek included. Companion CD available. Available as a discounted two-book set (Autumn/Winter + Spring/Summer) with CD from WECAN. ISBN 978-0-9722238-0-5

name: ⭐ 4. Dancing Hand, Trotting Pony
detail: Wilma Ellersiek. Translated by Lyn and Kundry Willwerth. WECAN Books. Wider movement games alongside finger plays — including active animal movement games. Songs, movement verses and active circle games. Suitable for kindergarten through lower grades.

name: ⭐ 5. Gnomes and Giants, Pixies and Elves
detail: Wilma Ellersiek, completed after her death by colleagues including Lynn St Pierre. WECAN Books, 2014. The final volume — the imaginal world of gnomes, giants, pixies and elves. Lynn St Pierre completed Ellersiek's unfinished work after training directly with Kundry Willwerth in Stuttgart. A treasure of imaginative gesture play for kindergarten and lower grades.

name: ⭐ Complete Wilma Ellersiek Four-Book Set
detail: WECAN Books. All four primary volumes in one discounted set: Giving Love Bringing Joy · Gesture Games for Spring and Summer · Gesture Games for Autumn and Winter · Dancing Hand Trotting Pony. The complete year's collection. The best investment for any Waldorf early childhood teacher or parent.

name: Finger Plays — Mercury Press (56 finger games)
detail: Compiled by Mercury Press. Waldorf Publications. Overall top seller as of 2024. 56 finger games for children aged 3+. Rhymes and finger movements printed side by side. "A great antidote for television! Nimbleness in finger movement will translate in later life to nimbleness of thinking." Affordable, practical and widely loved. waldorfpublications.org

name: A Lifetime of Joy — Bronja Zahlingen
detail: WECAN Books. A rich collection of circle games, finger games, songs, verses and plays for puppets. One of the most beloved and comprehensive Waldorf early childhood activity collections. Used in kindergartens worldwide. waldorfearlychildhood.org/store

name: ⭐ Lynn St Pierre — Ellersiek Specialist & Spacial Dynamics Trainer (USA / International)
detail: USA (Pacific Northwest / Colorado). Certified trainer in the developmental movement for early childhood created by Wilma Ellersiek. Spacial Dynamics Teacher Trainer. Apprenticed with Kundry Willwerth — the primary English translator of Ellersiek's books — and was a member of the Stuttgart Hand Gesture Working Circle. Co-author of Gnomes and Giants, Pixies and Elves (WECAN, 2014). Presents developmental movement through loving touch, hand gesture and large movement plays at Waldorf teacher training centres, conferences and schools internationally. Faculty at Dancing Hands & Frolicking Voices (annual 2-year intensive with Laurie Clark). dancinghandsfrolickingvoices.org

name: ⭐ Sunbridge Institute — Movement and Singing in the Ellersiek Tradition
detail: Chestnut Ridge, New York. Annual summer course with Lynn St Pierre. Participants immerse in finger plays, circle games, singing in the Mood of the Fifth and rhythmical verse. Spacial Dynamics included as personal development practice. Full of experiential activities — participants leave ready to use the work immediately with children. sunbridge.edu/event/movement-singing-ellersiek-tradition

name: Kundry Willwerth (1932–2017) — Legacy
detail: A Waldorf kindergarten teacher for over 30 years. Founding member of the Stuttgart Hand Gesture Working Circle. Translated and edited all four Ellersiek books into English. Presented workshops in North America, Europe, Brazil and Australia and trained teacher-trainers in the USA, Canada, Brazil, Europe and Australia. Her legacy lives on through Lynn St Pierre and hundreds of trained teachers worldwide.

name: ⭐ Lavender's Blue Homeschool — Seasonal Finger Games (Free videos)
detail: lavendersbluehomeschool.com/blogs/magic-fingerplays — Seasonal fingerplays demonstrated on video for each season. Watch, learn, then share with your child. Excellent practical explanations of how fingerplays build multiple capacities simultaneously. Free.

name: Soul Blossom Kids — Fairy Fingerplays (Free)
detail: soulblossomkids.com — Waldorf-inspired fingerplays and hand games with video demonstrations including spring and summer fairy games. Free.

name: tiptoes-lightly.net — Reg Down (Free)
detail: Reg Down's generous site includes dozens of finger verses, action verses and seasonal poems for young children. One of the most complete free Waldorf early childhood resources online. tiptoes-lightly.net

name: cedarwoodschool.org — Verse & Song Collection (Free)
detail: Cedarwood Waldorf School. Free online collection of fingerplays and gesture verses organised by season. cedarwoodschool.org/buttercup/song-verse

name: YouTube — Waldorf finger games (Free)
detail: Many Waldorf teachers share finger games on YouTube — search "Waldorf finger plays," "Waldorf gesture games," "Ellersiek finger games" or "Waldorf circle time kindergarten." The Lambkin fingerplay and Fairy fingerplay videos are particularly good examples with pedagogical notes.

name: ⭐ cedarwoodschool.org
detail: Cedarwood Waldorf School's free online Song & Verse collection — seasonal verses, circle songs, blessing verses and fingerplays, organised by season. One of the most comprehensive free verse archives online.

name: ⭐ tiptoes-lightly.net
detail: Reg Down. 230+ free stories AND dozens of seasonal verses, poems and circle games sorted by age and grade. The most generous free Waldorf resource online.

name: waldorfteacherresources.com
detail: Verses and songs organised by grade and theme — Advent, Christmas, circle, fall, farming, festivals, math verses, remedial, seasonal, spring. Free to search and use.

name: earthschooling.info
detail: Basic Waldorf verses page — morning verse, afternoon song, story time song, meal blessing, transition verses. A quick reference for new Waldorf families.

name: Spindrift & Gateways — Wynstones Press
detail: The two essential seasonal verse and poem collections used in Waldorf kindergartens worldwide. Every verse is seasonal and developmentally appropriate. The most used print resource for early childhood verses.

name: All Year Round — Hawthorn Press
detail: Druitt, Fynes-Clinton & Rowling. THE seasonal festival book — stories, poems, crafts and verses for every season and festival throughout the year. Includes a wide range of traditional Waldorf verses by season.

name: ⭐ Quintenlieder — Music for Young Children in the Mood of the Fifth
detail: Julius Knierim. Rudolf Steiner College Press. THE foundational songbook for the mood of the fifth — for the very youngest children ages 0–5. Essential for all Waldorf kindergarten and parent-child teachers.

name: I Love to Be Me — Songs in the Mood of the Fifth
detail: Channa A. Seidenberg. Wynstones Press. Companion to Quintenlieder. More mood-of-the-fifth songs for very young children.

name: Merrily We Sing — Original Songs in the Mood of the Fifth
detail: Ilian Willwerth. Another beloved mood-of-the-fifth collection widely used in Waldorf kindergartens.

name: ⭐ Shepherd's Songbook — Grades 1, 2 and 3
detail: Elisabeth Lebret. Waldorf School Association of Ontario. THE classic songbook for early Waldorf grades. Pentatonic songs matched to the Grade 1–3 curriculum. Used in Waldorf schools worldwide for decades.

name: One for the Golden Sun — Pentatonic Songs
detail: Peter Oram. Starborn Books. Pentatonic songs for young children. Also: A Change in the Year — pentatonic songs by the same author.

name: ⭐ Dancing As We Sing
detail: Nancy Foster. WECAN. Seasonal circle plays and traditional singing games for young children. Inseparably linked to the Waldorf early childhood curriculum.

name: Let Us Form a Ring
detail: Nancy Foster. WECAN. Circle games, movement songs and seasonal verses for kindergarten. The companion to Dancing As We Sing.

name: ⭐ Singing Games for Families, Schools and Communities
detail: Anna Rainville & Laurie Clark. WECAN. A treasury of singing games weaving movement, song, community and seasonal rhythm for all ages. From two of the most experienced Waldorf music-movement educators in North America.

name: Songs for Young Children
detail: John C. Miles. Promethean Press. Also: Folksongs for the Pentatonic Flute by the same author. Portland, Oregon. prometheanpress.com

name: Spindrift / Gateways — Wynstones Press
detail: UK. The two essential seasonal verse and song collections used in Waldorf kindergartens worldwide. Every verse is seasonal and developmentally appropriate. Own both volumes.

name: All Year Round — Druitt, Fynes-Clinton & Rowling
detail: Hawthorn Press. Songs, verses, poems and crafts for every festival and season throughout the year. The complete seasonal family companion.

name: Gesture Games for Spring & Summer / Autumn & Winter
detail: Wilma Ellersiek. WECAN. Finger games and seasonal gesture poems — movement woven with verse. The gold standard for ages 0–5.

name: ⭐ Rudolf Steiner Archive — Calendar of the Soul Tool (Free)
detail: rsarchive.org/COTS · The most complete free online resource. The current week's verse is shown automatically (Northern and Southern Hemisphere). All 52 verses in multiple English translations (Ruth & Hans Pusch; Owen Barfield; Isabel Wyatt and others). German original alongside. Counter verses. Historical context. Search by week number or date. Completely free — a public charity project.

name: ⭐ AnthroposophyLA — Calendar of the Soul Verses with Commentary
detail: anthroposophyla.org/calendar-of-the-soul-verses · All 52 verses with selected images and commentary compiled by Eloise Krivosheia. "The selected images and commentary may help anyone to open the deep mysteries and rhythms in the verses." Beautiful and accessible. Free.

name: AnthroWiki — Calendar of the Soul
detail: en.anthro.wiki/Calendar_of_the_Soul · Comprehensive encyclopaedia article on the structure, history and practice of the Calendar of the Soul. Includes references to all major translations and secondary literature. Free.

name: Das Goetheanum — Research on the Calendar of the Soul
detail: dasgoetheanum.com · Research articles on working with the mirror verse and counter verse. For deeper study after one has worked with the verses for a year or more. Free online articles.

name: Rudolf Steiner Institute — Calendar Resources
detail: rudolfsteiner.org · Introductory articles and study guides for the Calendar of the Soul. Good starting point for those new to the practice. Free PDF downloads available.

name: GA 40 — The Calendar of the Soul (Print)
detail: Rudolf Steiner. Translated by Ruth and Hans Pusch. Anthroposophic Press, 1982. The essential print edition — both German original and English translation with notes. Available via SteinerBooks, AbeBooks and rsarchive.org (free digital). ISBN 0-88010-263-2
