name: Rudolf Steiner (1861–1925)
detail: Initiated curative education through his 1924 Curative Education Course (12 lectures) — now published as Education for Special Needs (Rudolf Steiner Press). His foundational text. Steiner's core insight: every child's spiritual individuality is whole; outer difficulties are an opportunity for the teacher's own inner development as much as the child's. rsarchive.org for free online access.

name: Dr. Karl König (1902–1966)
detail: Austrian pediatrician and educator. Fled Nazi annexation in 1939 to Scotland. Founded the first Camphill Community in Aberdeen, Scotland, 1940. Expanded curative education globally — over 100 Camphill communities now exist worldwide. Core conviction: focus on each person's abilities, not disabilities. Key books: The First Three Years of the Child; Eternal Childhood; The Human Soul; Brothers and Sisters; Autism: Medical, Educational and Social Issues. Karl König Archive maintained by Camphill Academy.

name: Ita Wegman MD (1876–1943)
detail: Co-founder of anthroposophic medicine with Steiner. Her medical insights directly inform curative education — especially therapeutic movements, compresses and remedies for children with developmental challenges. Klinik Arlesheim (Switzerland) still carries this work.

name: ⭐ Robyn M. Brown — The Mulberry Centre for Curative Education
detail: Gold Beach, Oregon, USA. 33+ years Waldorf teacher. Founded Mulberry Classroom 2001; now The Mulberry Centre for Curative Education. Offers 3-year Curative Education Training Program for teachers and parents worldwide. Faculty at BACWTT and Center for Anthroposophy. Author: A Practical Guide to Curative Education: The Ladder of the Seven Life Processes (Lindisfarne Books, 440 pp). Mentors schools and teachers internationally. Website: themulberrycenterforcurativeeducation.org

name: Camphill Academy
detail: North America (camphill.edu). Professional education and certification in Anthroposophic Curative Education, Social Therapy and Social Agriculture. Practice-integrated — students live and learn within Camphill communities. Three concentrations: Curative Education (for those working with children/youth); Social Therapy (adults/elders); Social Agriculture & Biodynamics. Partners with Alanus University (Germany) for B.A. in Heilpädagogik and Antioch University for MEd in Healing Education. Member of NY State NCCRS credit recommendation service. Also supports the Karl König Archive.

name: Alanus University — Institute for Waldorf Education, Inclusion and Interculturality
detail: Alfter, Germany (alanus.edu). B.A. in Heilpädagogik (Curative Education). Partners with Camphill Academy North America for international training pathways. The academic home of professional curative education in Europe.

name: Center for Anthroposophy — Curative Education Renewal Course
detail: Wilton, New Hampshire. Annual renewal course with Robyn Brown (June/July). "Deepening Waldorf Education: Meeting and Understanding Every Child." Covers six curative polarities, twelve senses, and practical applications in classroom. centerforanthroposophy.org

name: Somerset School (Colfax, California)
detail: Sunny Baldwin's foundational programme. Where Robyn Brown apprenticed. A curative school where "children who came got better — healing happened." The model that inspired Mulberry Classroom. Based directly on Steiner's Curative Education lectures.

name: SECA — Steiner Education Curative Approach (Australia)
detail: Online training with Robyn Brown. Hosted curative education courses for Australian and Asia-Pacific Waldorf community. steinerearlychildhood.com

name: Antioch University — MEd Healing Education
detail: Wilton, NH / Keene, NH. 32-credit master's program; transdisciplinary focus on Healing Education; for experienced Waldorf educators and anthroposophic practitioners. antioch.edu

name: Robyn M. Brown
detail: Curative education training, mentoring and workshops internationally. The Mulberry Centre. Author: A Practical Guide to Curative Education. themulberrycenterforcurativeeducation.org

name: Henning Köhler
detail: Germany. Author: Working with Anxious, Nervous and Depressed Children; The Inner Life of the Earth. Curative educator and anthroposophical psychotherapist. Translated into many languages. Practical tools for parents and teachers. AWSNA / Floris Books.

name: Susan Perrow MEd
detail: Australia. Therapeutic storytelling for challenging behaviour and difficult situations. Online training; individual mentoring; books translated into 10+ languages. susanperrow.com

name: Kim John Payne MEd
detail: USA/Australia. Simplicity Parenting; Social Inclusion Approach (breaking patterns of exclusion and bullying — 200+ schools); drug-free research on attention disorders; Waldorf Community Collaborative Counseling at Antioch. School counselor + family therapist for 20+ years. simplicityparenting.com

name: Audrey McAllen — The Extra Lesson
detail: UK. Developed The Extra Lesson — movement-based remedial work for children with learning difficulties. A widely used therapeutic program in Waldorf schools. Her book The Extra Lesson (Hawthorn Press) is a key resource for remedial Waldorf specialists. Eikonboom has continued this research (Floris Books).

name: Susan Johnson MD
detail: USA. Waldorf-aligned paediatric developmentalist. Widely referenced by Waldorf schools and PAAM. Articles on sensory nutrition, child development and healing childhood. Advocates screen-free, movement-rich early childhood.

name: Peter Selg
detail: Switzerland. Director of the Ita Wegman Institute. Curative education scholar. Author: The Essence of Waldorf Education; many titles on Steiner's curative work. "From its very beginning, curative education was an integral part of the original Waldorf school in Stuttgart." (Selg)

name: Nettie Fabrie
detail: Netherlands. Remedial specialist and Waldorf teacher trainer. Co-author Making Math Meaningful (Grades 1–5). Remedial programme director at Seattle Waldorf School. Faculty Sound Circle Center. Mentored teachers in Netherlands, Czech Republic and USA. Expert in bridging curative approaches with mainstream Waldorf teaching.

name: Patti Connolly
detail: USA. Student Support Teacher (Early Childhood–Grade 3); remedial specialist; 30+ years. Currently at Waldorf School of the Roaring Fork, Colorado. Mentors Kindergarten–4th Grade teachers. waldorfinspirations.com

name: LifeWays North America
detail: USA. Child care and early childhood training. Supports caregivers and parents with Waldorf/curative approaches for young children. Articles on therapeutic lens on challenging behaviours. lifewaysnorthamerica.org

name: Education for Special Needs (Curative Education Course)
detail: Rudolf Steiner. 12 lectures from 1924. The foundational text. Every curative educator begins here. Available free online via rsarchive.org; in print via Rudolf Steiner Press.

name: A Practical Guide to Curative Education: The Ladder of the Seven Life Processes
detail: Robyn M. Brown. 440 pages. The most accessible, practical modern guide to Steiner's curative education. For both parents and teachers. "A much-needed reminder of a tried-and-tested approach that can work for every child."

name: Healing Stories for Challenging Behaviour
detail: Susan Perrow. The go-to therapeutic storytelling resource. Translated into 10+ languages. Custom story framework for specific child behaviours.

name: Therapeutic Storytelling: 101 Healing Stories for Children
detail: Susan Perrow. 101 stories for behaviour, grief, anxiety, bullying, bedwetting and more. With story-writing framework.

name: Stories to Light the Night
detail: Susan Perrow. Stories for grief, loss, separation, death, divorce, pet loss, ecological grief. 94 stories from multiple cultures.

name: An A-Z Collection of Behaviour Tales: From Angry Ant to Zestless Zebra
detail: Susan Perrow. Illustrated alphabet of behaviour stories — quick reference by specific challenge.

name: Working with Anxious, Nervous and Depressed Children
detail: Henning Köhler. Germany. Understanding and supporting children with emotional difficulties from an anthroposophic perspective. Practical tools for parents and teachers.

name: The Extra Lesson
detail: Audrey McAllen. Movement-based remedial programme for learning difficulties. Specific sequences for reading, writing, arithmetic challenges.

name: The Twelve Senses
detail: Albert Soesman (Netherlands). Steiner's twelve senses clearly explained. Understanding sensory difficulties through the curative lens.

name: Children with a Difference: Background of Steiner Special Education
detail: Walter Holtzapfel. Overview of Steiner's approach to various developmental differences.

name: Children with Special Needs: Rudolf Steiner's Approach
detail: Michael Luxford. Practical guide to applying Steiner's insights in special needs settings.

name: Autism: Medical, Educational and Social Issues
detail: Karl König. Perspective on autism from the founder of Camphill. Historic and still relevant.

name: Education for Special Needs (Kolisko-related research)
detail: Multiple AWSNA and Floris publications; Waldorf Research Bulletin volumes on special education.

name: Simplicity Parenting
detail: Kim John Payne. For children on the "behaviour spectrum" — reducing stress, establishing rhythm, social inclusion. Applicable to all children but particularly powerful for children with attention and social difficulties.

name: The Soul of Discipline
detail: Kim John Payne. Warm, firm and calm guidance from toddlers to teens. Simplicity Parenting approach for families navigating challenging behaviour.

name: Dr. Adam Blanning MD ★
detail: Denver, CO, USA. Board-certified family medicine + certified anthroposophic medicine. Author: Raising Sound Sleepers (2024). Works with Waldorf schools as educational and developmental consultant. PAAM Co-Leader. Denver Center for Anthroposophic Therapies. Key resource for parents navigating developmental challenges with an anthroposophic medical lens.

name: Dr. Michaela Glöckler MD
detail: Germany/Switzerland. Formerly head of Medical Section, Goetheanum. A Waldorf Guide to Children's Health; The Dignity of the Young Child. International voice on child development, vaccines and healthy childhood. The key paediatric medical author for Waldorf-aligned families.

name: Susan Johnson MD
detail: USA. Paediatric developmentalist. Articles on sensory nutrition, screen time, learning difficulties and healthy development through a Waldorf-aligned lens. Widely referenced in Waldorf school support departments.
